snapshot.title: Public alpha repo hardening
snapshot.body:
Prepare DaCWatch for public alpha release aimed at developers comfortable launching a macOS GUI app from the command line.

Why:
- The product is already functional and well-tested, but the repo still needs release-engineering, onboarding, and polish work before public viewing.
- This epic tracks the initial hardening pass before opening the repo publicly.

Scope:
- Packaging/release hygiene
- CI
- README/product presentation
- Kroki onboarding and failure UX
- Preferences persistence
- Logging / diagnostics
- Contributor-facing repo docs

Done looks like:
- Child beans under this epic are complete or explicitly descoped for alpha.
- Repo is in a state where a public alpha README and issue tracker would feel intentional rather than accidental.

snapshot.title: Packaging and metadata cleanup for public alpha
snapshot.body:
Clean up Python packaging and release metadata so the project looks intentional to outside users.

What to change:
- Remove test-only packages such as pytest from runtime dependencies in pyproject.toml.
- Add richer project metadata: authors/maintainers, classifiers, repository/homepage/issues URLs, better short description if needed.
- Sanity-check wheel/sdist output for public distribution expectations.
- Review .gitignore / tracked artifacts so local dev files are less likely to leak into public commits.

Relevant files:
- pyproject.toml
- README.md
- .gitignore
- any release/build config files

Done looks like:
- Runtime dependencies contain only runtime requirements.
- Package metadata is suitable for PyPI/public repo viewing.
- Build output has been validated and obvious release hygiene issues are addressed.

snapshot.title: Add GitHub Actions CI for tests and build sanity
snapshot.body:
Add minimal CI so public viewers can trust the codebase health.

What to change:
- Create GitHub Actions workflow(s) that run tests on push and pull request.
- Prefer macOS coverage because the app is macOS-first; Linux may be included for extra confidence if practical.
- Include a packaging/build step to ensure wheel/sdist creation still works.

Relevant files:
- .github/workflows/*
- README.md if adding badges

Done looks like:
- A public PR would automatically run tests.
- CI covers the main supported environment and catches packaging regressions.

snapshot.title: Strengthen README for public alpha onboarding and positioning
snapshot.body:
Improve the README so a new developer immediately understands what DaCWatch is, who it is for, how to install/use it, and what rough edges to expect.

What to change:
- Add or improve sections for audience/positioning, alpha expectations, and known rough edges.
- Add visual proof such as screenshots or a short demo GIF/video link.
- Keep the install/run story clear for users who will launch the app from the command line.
- Incorporate any newly added install guidance (for example global editable installs) into a cohesive onboarding flow.

Relevant files:
- README.md
- image/demo assets if added

Done looks like:
- README gives a strong first impression for public alpha visitors.
- A new user can tell whether the tool is for them in under a minute.

snapshot.title: Improve Kroki startup and connection failure UX
snapshot.body:
Make the app friendlier when Kroki is unavailable or misconfigured, since this is likely the main first-run failure mode.

What to change:
- Add startup validation or health-check behavior for the configured Kroki endpoint.
- Improve user-facing error messaging and recovery hints for unreachable endpoints, timeouts, and bad responses.
- Provide explicit next steps such as starting the bundled self-hosted stack or using the public kroki.io endpoint.
- Add tests for the expected failure paths.

Relevant files:
- src/dacwatch/kroki_client.py
- src/dacwatch/app.py
- src/dacwatch/main.py
- tests related to CLI/app/Kroki client
- README.md troubleshooting/setup sections

Done looks like:
- First-run failures are diagnosed clearly.
- Users get actionable remediation steps instead of generic errors.

snapshot.title: Persist user preferences beyond window geometry
snapshot.body:
Add preference persistence for common user-visible controls so the app feels less stateless between runs.

What to change:
- Decide which settings should persist for alpha, likely including render format preference, auto-scale, and always-on-top where applicable.
- Extend existing persistence/state handling or add dedicated config storage.
- Add tests covering save/load behavior and reasonable defaults.
- Document the behavior in README if needed.

Relevant files:
- src/dacwatch/window_manager.py
- src/dacwatch/app.py
- UI/window classes
- tests for window manager / preferences

Done looks like:
- User preferences survive restarts.
- Persistence logic is tested and documented.

snapshot.title: Replace print-based diagnostics with structured logging and CLI verbosity flags
snapshot.body:
Upgrade diagnostics from ad hoc print statements to a more deliberate logging approach suitable for public alpha support.

What to change:
- Replace print calls with Python logging (or equivalent structured approach).
- Add CLI flags such as --verbose and/or --debug.
- Keep default output clean while making troubleshooting output easy to enable.
- Ensure startup, watcher events, render failures, and shutdown paths log clearly.

Relevant files:
- src/dacwatch/main.py
- src/dacwatch/app.py
- src/dacwatch/file_watcher.py
- tests/test_cli.py and any affected tests
- README.md usage/troubleshooting sections

Done looks like:
- Normal runs are quiet and polished.
- Debug information is available on demand for issue reports.

snapshot.title: Add contributor docs and issue templates for public alpha
snapshot.body:
Add the lightweight repo scaffolding that makes public collaboration easier from day one.

What to change:
- Add CONTRIBUTING.md with local setup, test command, and notes about manual GUI validation.
- Add GitHub issue templates for bug reports and feature requests.
- Optionally add PR guidance if that seems useful at alpha stage.

Relevant files:
- CONTRIBUTING.md
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*
- .github/pull_request_template.md (optional)

Done looks like:
- Outside contributors know how to run tests and report useful bugs.
- The repo has basic public-collaboration hygiene.
